title: Experiential Continuity in Human-AI Interaction
subtitle: A Single-Profile Multi-Tier Architecture — Martin Grobbelaar, July 2026

sections.heading: The Paper
sections.content: Most AI assistants treat every session as a fresh start. This paper argues that the real problem isn't model capability — it's experiential continuity: the user's investment in shaping the interaction should compound, not reset. We present a single-profile, multi-tier architecture where one persistent identity accumulates memory, skills, and interaction history across every session, delegating specialised work behind the scenes. A three-month case study demonstrates zero re-explanation cycles, accumulated skill growth, and machine-independent recovery. The paper's one-sentence claim: “This practitioner position paper proposes that experiential continuity — not just memory or delegation — is the missing dimension in human-AI interaction, and presents a single-profile multi-tier architecture validated through three months of daily use, with unplanned convergence toward cognitive-architecture patterns observed and offered for falsification.”

sections.heading: Key Findings
items: The architecture independently arrived at organisational patterns — memory hierarchies, impasse-driven escalation, procedural chunking — that mirror decades of cognitive architecture research (Soar, ACT-R). Presented as an observation inviting falsification: if it holds, experiential continuity is a structural requirement for natural-feeling interaction, not a luxury feature

Consistency as a directional pattern: across pilot runs (N=3), the evolved condition stayed within an observed ±1 API call range while the blank agent spread 2.9× — a structural scaffold hinting at reduced stochastic behaviour, pending larger-N validation

Production-grade patterns: the evolved agent produced Alembic migrations, Docker Compose, Material M3 theming, and zoneless Angular — patterns the blank and configured conditions never exhibited despite access to the same base model
User efficiency: zero re-explanation cycles across three months of daily use. What the user teaches once, the system remembers forever

Two valid specialist patterns identified: Script-Bridged (lightweight, no tool access) and Spawned Subagent (full tool access, structured delegation) — both implement the same protocol at different capability–cost points

Integrity Verification Gates (IVGs) — a proposed methodological protocol for anchoring continuity and ethical claims to independently verifiable state checkpoints, now being applied to the system's own deployments

sections.heading: The Architecture
sections.content: Three active tiers share one identity: a Primary (interaction holder, orchestrator, memory and ethics), a Light Specialist (local Hermes 3 8B via script-bridged pattern, zero cost), and a Deep Specialist (top-tier model via spawned subagent pattern, on-demand). A Scheduler handles automated background routines. Specialists are intentionally stateless — they receive task briefs, execute, and return results. Only the Primary knows who the user is.

sections.heading: The Quote That Says It All
sections.content: "It knew my name but not who I was. It answered questions but never got better. Every conversation was day one." — the user, comparing the evolved profile against a stateless interface running the same underlying model.
